title: Walk to where the command leads: the destination_v9 locomotion model
summary: We gave the walking policy a ghost: the pose each command would reach, with its heading, as input and as reward, then tightened that reward, added a matching heading reward and doubled the joint penalties, and finally fine-tuned it on stopping after a walk. The resulting destination_v9 checkpoint passes all 13 native learning probes; after 20 s walks it ends 1.3 mm (median) and 1.8 mm (worst) from where the command leads and its heading drifts 0.09 degrees, against 151 mm, 298 mm and 16 degrees for the PR 71 model it started from. Five native Spark trainings lead to it, each from the previous checkpoint.
next: Review the destination_v9 lineage and decide whether it becomes the locomotion model; on acceptance, record it in the registry and promote its reward and stop schedule from the experiment registry into the canonical task.
